# Loose Ends

> Loose Ends is a one-person studio in Tunis, run by Houssem Gabsi. It builds websites, automation and content systems for established firms, in English, French and Arabic.

Based in Tunis. Works in English, French and Arabic.

Site: https://houssem-gabsi.vercel.app/

## Services

- Websites and applications.: The site clients judge the firm by and the tools the team opens every morning, designed and built end to end.
- Work that runs without anyone doing it.: Follow-up, confirmations and reports happen on their own. A person approves what matters before anything is sent.
- Identity and content.: A visual identity, and a content process that turns one idea into a week of publishing in the firm's own voice.

## Cases

Four pieces of client work. Clients are not named.

### Open roles entered once, live everywhere.

Executive search, Washington D.C.

Roles go into the firm's recruiting system and appear on its eighteen-page website without anyone retyping them. Candidate CVs are put into the firm's format in one step. The same database now answers the team's questions through their AI assistant.

Status: Website live. Candidate scoring in development.

### A nineteenth-century house that looks like itself online.

Maison d'hôte, La Marsa

An identity drawn by hand from the house's own tiles, doors and objects. It runs through a website in French and English and the printed pieces guests hold, from the room card to the table d'hôte menu.

Status: Identity and print delivered. Website in development.

### A class booked on one screen, not in a message thread.

Yoga studio, Tunis

Schedule, places and payment sit on a single phone screen, in French and English. Bookings moved out of Instagram messages and into one place.

Status: Live.

### An AI assistant that works the way he does.

Journalist, video production

His assistant is set up around his editorial week, not the software's defaults. The tasks he repeats now run the same way every time, with video production at the centre.

Status: Delivered 2026.

## Own products

### A recruiting platform that explains every score.

Vero, a web application that reads a batch of résumés against a role, ranks the candidates, and shows the reasoning and the source text behind every score. It also drafts outreach based on each candidate's own work. The decision stays with a person.

Status: Live.

Link: https://vero-woad.vercel.app/

### A daily entry-risk score for stocks and crypto.

ZonedInOut, a website that scores stocks, ETFs and cryptocurrencies every trading day on how far the price has moved from its average, with an entry zone and a stop level for each. Past calls are published and graded. It is a scoring system, not financial advice.

Status: Live.

Link: https://zonedinout.vercel.app/

## Systems

- Every unanswered enquiry, found and drafted.: The system reads the inbox, quotes and invoices, finds what went quiet, and drafts each reply. Someone approves, then it sends. Status: Built. Demonstrated on a fictional firm.
- Every candidate read against the search.: Each candidate is assessed against that search's own criteria, with the reasoning written beside the score. The recruiter decides. Status: In development for an executive search firm.
- One idea, a week of publishing.: A researched article and a week of posts from a single idea. Every figure is checked against a named source before it goes out. Status: In weekly use on client work.
- Interview notes in, client report out.: Raw notes become a finished report in the firm's format. Every rating points to its source, and gaps are flagged, never filled. Status: Built. Demonstrated on fictional data.

## How an engagement starts

1. Find the loose end. A free one-page review of where the firm loses time. No call required.
2. Measure it. A paid audit ranks the first three fixes by what they return. The fee is credited toward the build.
3. Build one thing. The fix with the most hours in it, at one price agreed in writing.
